subproblem.title: H^n-null sets on which μ has finite density are μ-null
subproblem.statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N and Z ⊆ ℝ^N with H^n(Z) = 0 such that at every x ∈ Z the n-density of μ exists and is finite (HasDensity n μ x θ for some θ ∈ [0, ∞)). Then μ(Z) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (Z : Set (Euclidean N)), μHE[n] Z = 0 → (∀ x ∈ Z, ∃ θ : ℝ≥0∞, θ ≠ ∞ ∧ HasDensity n μ x θ) → μ Z = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step (3a) of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (the covering comparison of Ch. 1, 3.2(2): if Θ^{*n}(μ, x) ≤ t on A then μ(A) ≤ 2^n t H^n(A)). Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; μH[n] is Mathlib's (unnormalised) n-dimensional Hausdorff measure and H^n := μHE[n] = c_n · μH[n] with c_n ∈ (0, ∞) (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def); diam is the extended diameter, and ENNReal powers satisfy 0^0 = 1.

1. Decomposition. For k ∈ ℕ and j ≥ 1 let Z_{k,j} := {x ∈ Z : μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ (k + 1) ω ρ^n for all ρ ∈ (0, 1/j]}. Then Z = ⋃_{k,j} Z_{k,j}: if x ∈ Z and HasDensity n μ x θ with θ < ∞, choose k ∈ ℕ with θ < k + 1; since densityRatio n μ x ρ → θ as ρ ↓ 0, there is j ≥ 1 with densityRatio n μ x ρ < k + 1 for all ρ ∈ (0, 1/j], and as ω · ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n ∈ (0, ∞) for ρ > 0 this gives μ(B_ρ(x)) < (k + 1) ω ρ^n. By countable subadditivity it suffices to show μ(Z_{k,j}) = 0 for all k, j.

2. Fix k, j, put δ := 1/j and c := (k + 1) ω < ∞. Since Z_{k,j} ⊆ Z, H^n(Z_{k,j}) = 0, hence μH[n](Z_{k,j}) = 0 (c_n ≠ 0).

3. Covers. By Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply (MeasureTheory/Measure/Hausdorff.lean:546), μH[n](Z_{k,j}) = ⨆_{r>0} ⨅ {Σ_i ⨆_{t_i ≠ ∅} diam(t_i)^n : Z_{k,j} ⊆ ⋃_i t_i, diam t_i ≤ r ∀ i}. As this is 0, for r := ENNReal.ofReal δ and every ζ > 0 the inner infimum is < ζ, so there is a sequence (t_i)_{i∈ℕ} with Z_{k,j} ⊆ ⋃_i t_i, diam t_i ≤ δ for all i, and Σ_{i : t_i ≠ ∅} diam(t_i)^n < ζ.

4. One covering set. Let i be such that t_i ∩ Z_{k,j} ≠ ∅; pick x_i ∈ t_i ∩ Z_{k,j} and put d_i := diam t_i ∈ [0, δ]. Then t_i ⊆ B_{d_i}(x_i). Claim: μ(t_i ∩ Z_{k,j}) ≤ c · d_i^n.
 – If d_i > 0: μ(t_i ∩ Z_{k,j}) ≤ μ(B_{d_i}(x_i)) ≤ c d_i^n, because d_i ∈ (0, δ] and x_i ∈ Z_{k,j}.
 – If d_i = 0: t_i = {x_i} and μ({x_i}) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x_i)) ≤ c ρ^n for every ρ ∈ (0, δ]. For n ≥ 1, letting ρ ↓ 0 gives μ({x_i}) = 0 = c · 0^n; for n = 0 it gives μ({x_i}) ≤ c = c · 0^0.

5. Summation. Sets t_i not meeting Z_{k,j} contribute nothing, so by countable subadditivity μ(Z_{k,j}) ≤ Σ_i μ(t_i ∩ Z_{k,j}) ≤ c Σ_{i : t_i ≠ ∅} diam(t_i)^n ≤ c ζ. Since ζ > 0 is arbitrary and c < ∞, μ(Z_{k,j}) = 0. By 1, μ(Z) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Z is the countable union of Z_{k,j} = {μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ (k+1)ω_nρ^n for 0 < ρ ≤ 1/j} by finiteness of the density.
H^n(Z_{k,j}) = 0 gives covers by sets of diameter ≤ 1/j with Σ diam^n < ζ (hausdorffMeasure_apply).
Each covering set meeting Z_{k,j} lies in a ball B_{d_i}(x_i) with μ ≤ (k+1)ω_n d_i^n (degenerate d_i = 0 handled separately).

audit.reason: Finite densities give the stated countable decomposition with uniform ball bounds. Hausdorff-null covers and summation force zero measure, with zero-diameter covering sets handled for both zero and positive dimensions. No unstated regularity or sigma-finiteness is needed.
